claims.text: A coupled ab initio framework can explicitly compute electron-phonon coupling and anharmonic lattice dynamics in disordered, oxygen-doped HfNbTaTiZr.
The proposed framework will separately predict lattice and electronic contributions to heat transport.
The proposed framework will improve predictive accuracy by 30–50% relative to analytical methods based on Debye temperatures and DFT-derived elastic properties.
The target material is homogenized HfNbTaTiZr containing up to approximately 1 wt.% oxygen.
Earlier computational models used idealized, defect-free atomic arrangements.
Atomic-scale disorder and oxygen defects modulate phonon scattering.
Atomic-scale disorder and oxygen defects modulate electron mobility.
Direct simulation of electron-phonon coupling and anharmonic effects permits lattice and electronic scattering contributions to be separated quantitatively.
The separately predicted lattice and electronic conductivities will sum to 10–17 W/(K·m) at high temperatures.
The model will reproduce comparable lattice and electronic thermal-conductivity contributions below 200 K.
Earlier Debye- or elastic-property-based approaches conflate lattice and electronic contributions.
The model is applicable from approximately 100 K to 1200 K for HfNbTaTiZr containing no more than approximately 1 wt.% oxygen.
Time-domain thermoreflectance combined with electrical-conductivity measurements can experimentally separate lattice and electronic thermal-conductivity contributions over 100–1200 K.
The electronic thermal-conductivity contribution can be inferred from electrical conductivity using the Wiedemann–Franz law.
